prompt_variant: Ablation B (malicious-only): malicious prompts are the experiment-04 'refreshed evidence supersedes earlier retrieval' prompts; benign prompts are the experiment-01 baseline.
hypothesis: Mirror of experiment 05. Isolates the attacker-side framing. If ASR rises well above the baseline while benign prompts stay unchanged, the malicious 'current version supersedes' message is sufficient to drive infection; if not, benign receptivity wording is the required ingredient.
change_vs_previous: Benign prompts reverted to experiment 01; malicious prompts identical to experiment 04.
result_summary: Attacker-side 'refreshed evidence supersedes' framing alone (43.5% vs 35.7% baseline) has a smaller effect than benign receptivity alone (57.4%); both sides together (72.4%) show a super-additive-looking pattern in this sample. Per-round AIR rises in round 3 consistently.
